ai_technology: Random forest and nested group-aware MEG connectivity classification

evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers map multi-band wPLI connectivity to case/control labels; SHAP characterizes model contributions.
evidence.tested: Nested group-aware internal cross-validation in 70 participants, keeping all data from each subject together and tuning inside training folds.
evidence.unknown: No external clinical performance or mechanism established; high fold variance and small cohort limit interpretation.

organization: Beihang University; Qilu Hospital of Shandong University; Shandong First Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript: cohort definition, actual model/input/preprocessing/split Methods and reported classification Results/limitations. No prospective utility claim.

summary: A preprint evaluated subject-level MEG connectivity classifiers in 39 lumbar-stenosis patients and 31 controls. Random forest achieved mean nested-cross-validation AUC 0.723 with fold standard deviation 0.262, indicating substantial uncertainty and variation. SHAP identified features contributing to model discrimination; independently tested physiological group differences are separate results, not all AI-discovered mechanisms. The small cross-sectional study provides neither external validation nor clinical diagnostic utility.
title: MEG connectivity classifier shows limited lumbar-stenosis discrimination
